title: Kenney 1-Bit Pack
lede: Kenney’s public-domain sheet of more than 1,000 game tiles draws every tree, wall, monster, weapon, icon, and letter on a 16-pixel grid with a few flat colors.
summary: A tilesheet of one-color 16 × 16 icons, tiles, and letters on dark plum, with a few accent colors. Kenney, 2019–2020, CC0.
made: Posted on OpenGameArt 6 May 2019; version 1.1 dated 6 May 2020 in its License.txt

evidence.note: Downloaded `1bitpack_kenney_1.1.zip` from the OpenGameArt page and inspected `Tilesheet/colored_packed.png` (768 × 352 px) enlarged 2× to 1536 × 704 px. The file has exactly 8 colors. The sample map on the page was not used, because it is resampled (254 colors) and carries a license banner.

styles.note: A complete low-resolution sprite and tile vocabulary: whole-pixel shapes on a 16-pixel grid, an 8-color palette, a bitmap alphabet, and game items such as hearts, keys, coins, and cards.

context: OpenGameArt describes the pack as more than 1,000 tiles, characters, objects, and items for roguelike and RPG games, with tiles for UI, platformers, and puzzle games, a monochrome version, and transparent versions. [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org/content/1-bit-pack).

The License.txt in the download says “Created/distributed by Kenney (www.kenney.nl)”, “Creation date: 06-05-2020”, and “License: (Creative Commons Zero, CC0)”. The OpenGameArt page shows the submission date 6 May 2019, so the 2020 date is probably version 1.1. [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org/content/1-bit-pack).
observed: A dense grid of 16 × 16 tiles on a dark plum ground (#472d3c).
Most tiles are one flat light color (#cfc6b8): characters, skulls, swords, bows, walls, fences, furniture, and frames.
A few groups use one accent each: green trees and plants, blue water, brown furniture, red bricks and playing cards, yellow coins and crowns.
The sheet has a full bitmap alphabet and digits, arrows, hearts, crosses, dice, and warning signs at the lower right.
Shading is absent. Each sprite is a silhouette with interior lines cut out of it.
All diagonals, such as the swords and the diamond frame, step one pixel at a time.
interpretation: The pack shows the most reduced form of the style: one color per object and one pixel unit for everything. It reads as game art without any shading.
The sheet is also a ready inventory of the game furniture that the rubric names: hearts, coins, keys, cursors, frames, and a pixel alphabet.
borrow: Draw icons as one-color silhouettes on a 16-pixel grid, and color each family of icons with one accent.
Use a dark, slightly warm ground instead of pure black, so the light pixels read softly.

images.alt: A large grid of small one-color pixel tiles on dark plum: trees, buildings, furniture, characters, monsters, weapons, potions, playing cards, arrows, hearts, and a pixel alphabet, mostly in off-white with green, blue, brown, red, and yellow accents.
